credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

customer_ref.description: `customer_ref` identifies a customer or customer job. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In SalesReceipt and ReceivePayment, it identifies who receives credit. In TimeTracking, it identifies who the time can be billed to and is required in TimeTrackingAdd when IsBillable is true.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a BillAddress or ShipAddress aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

vendor_ref.description: A vendor is any person or company from whom a small business owner buys goods and services. (Banks and tax agencies usually are included on the vendor list.) A company’s vendor list contains information such as account balance and contact information about each vendor. A `vendor_ref` aggregate refers to one of the vendors on the list.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

is_to_be_printed.description: If `is_to_be_printed` is true, QuickBooks queues the form for later printing. It does not print immediately; printing is still a user action in QuickBooks.

ref_number.description: `ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

ap_account_ref.description: Refers to an accounts payable account in the QuickBooks file. (The AccountType of this account will be AccountsPayable.) iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. On by default, with pages of 100 records (25 with `include_line_items`); send `iterator=true` with `max_returned` for another size. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

max_returned.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.) If you include a `max_returned` value, it must be at least 1.

The page size, with `iterator=true`. Sent without `iterator`, or with `iterator=false`, it's a cap instead: at most this many records come back, in one answer, and QuickBooks doesn't say whether more matched.

meta_data.description: Use the `meta_data` attribute to control whether query responses include counts. from_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00.

to_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or before this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to end-of-day (23:59:59).

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for `full_name` and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants.

full_name_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants. For names that don’t have children, `full_name_with_children` is exactly the same as `full_name`.

currency_filter.description:

include_line_items.description: This filter allows you to omit line items from a query response to get a smaller result. The default value is false, so line items are omitted by default. Set `include_line_items` to true to include line items in the response if you don’t mind getting a larger result.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. On by default, with pages of 100 records (25 with `include_line_items`); send `iterator=true` with `max_returned` for another size. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

max_returned.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.) If you include a `max_returned` value, it must be at least 1.

The page size, with `iterator=true`. Sent without `iterator`, or with `iterator=false`, it's a cap instead: at most this many records come back, in one answer, and QuickBooks doesn't say whether more matched.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

meta_data.description: Use the `meta_data` attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). Counts are approximate and may vary slightly if records are created or deleted during processing.

modified_date_range_filter.description:
Filters according to the dates when transactions were last modified. The `modified_date_range_filter` aggregate isn’t required to contain any elements, but if it is empty, we recommend that you leave it out altogether. Note that the time portion of the `from_modified_date` and `to_modified_date` fields wasn’t supported in qbXML version 1.0 or 1.1.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

from_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00.

to_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or before this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to end-of-day (23:59:59).

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

ref_number.description:
`ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Filters according to the original transaction dates.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). from_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or after this date. Both `from_txn_date` and `to_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999.If you omit `from_txn_date`, it will be set to 1970-01-01 (1969-12-31 PST).

to_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or before this date. Both `to_txn_date` and `from_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999. If you omit `to_txn_date`, it will be set to 2038-01-19 (2038-01-18 PST).

date_macro.description: `date_macro` filters by transaction date (not last-modified date). Do not combine `date_macro` with `from_modified_date`/`to_modified_date` in the same query filter set.

txn_id.description:
`txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because `owner_id` and `data_ext_name` together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same `owner_id` of zero, the `data_ext_name` must be a unique value among existing custom fields.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

entity_filter.description:
An entity refers to a person on the QuickBooks Customer list, Vendor list, Employee list, or Other Names list. You can use an EntityQuery request to get information about all the entities that are set up in the QuickBooks file. In an ARRefundCreditCard query, this must be a customer/customer job.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

list_id_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants.

full_name_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants. For names that don’t have children, `full_name_with_children` is exactly the same as `full_name`.

include_line_items.description: This filter allows you to omit line items from a query response to get a smaller result. The default value is false, so line items are omitted by default. Set `include_line_items` to true to include line items in the response if you don’t mind getting a larger result.

include_linked_txns.description: If you set `include_linked_txns` to true, then the returned object will include a list of all the transactions linked to the queried object. (This list is similar to the History view of a transaction in the user interface, but not identical, as the SDK list contains only linked transactions, not items.) Each linked transaction will be represented by a `linked_txn` aggregate.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. On by default, with pages of 100 records (25 with `include_line_items` or `include_linked_txns`); send `iterator=true` with `max_returned` for another size. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

max_returned.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.) If you include a `max_returned` value, it must be at least 1.

The page size, with `iterator=true`. Sent without `iterator`, or with `iterator=false`, it's a cap instead: at most this many records come back, in one answer, and QuickBooks doesn't say whether more matched.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

meta_data.description: Use the `meta_data` attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). Counts are approximate and may vary slightly if records are created or deleted during processing.

modified_date_range_filter.description:
Filters according to the dates when transactions were last modified. The `modified_date_range_filter` aggregate isn’t required to contain any elements, but if it is empty, we recommend that you leave it out altogether. Note that the time portion of the `from_modified_date` and `to_modified_date` fields wasn’t supported in qbXML version 1.0 or 1.1.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

from_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00.

to_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or before this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to end-of-day (23:59:59).

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

ref_number.description:
`ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

ref_number_case_sensitive.description: Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

ref_number_filter.description:

to_ref_number.description: The final `ref_number` in the search range. If `to_ref_number` is omitted, the range will end with last number on the list.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

txn_date_range_filter.description:
Filters according to the original transaction dates.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

from_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or after this date. Both `from_txn_date` and `to_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999.If you omit `from_txn_date`, it will be set to 1970-01-01 (1969-12-31 PST).

to_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or before this date. Both `to_txn_date` and `from_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999. If you omit `to_txn_date`, it will be set to 2038-01-19 (2038-01-18 PST).

date_macro.description: `date_macro` filters by transaction date (not last-modified date). Do not combine `date_macro` with `from_modified_date`/`to_modified_date` in the same query filter set.

txn_id.description:
`txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

fob.description: QuickBooks uses the term FOB, “freight on board,” to indicate the place from which the product is shipped. The FOB has no accounting implications.

is_pending.description: If `is_pending` is set to true, the credit memo hasn’t been completed. Within QuickBooks, you can change the `is_pending` status for a credit memo by choosing “Mark Credit Memo As Pending” or “Mark Credit Memo As Final” from the Edit menu.

is_tax_included.description: For future use with international versions of QuickBooks.

is_to_be_emailed.description: When enabled, QuickBooks validates the customer email at runtime before sending. If no valid email is available, the request fails.

is_to_be_printed.description: If `is_to_be_printed` is true, QuickBooks queues the form for later printing. It does not print immediately; printing is still a user action in QuickBooks.

item_sales_tax_ref.description: An ItemSalesTax entry represents one tax rate paid to one tax agency. Use it when a transaction needs a single tax calculation. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in `ship_address_block` or `bill_address_block`.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

ship_date.description: The date when the product was, or will be, shipped.

currency_code.description: For built-in currencies, the currency code and name is the generally accepted code and name. These are based on the standard ISO 4217 code/name for a country’s currency. In most cases, the currency code is composed of the country’s two-character Internet country code plus an extra character representing the currency unit.

currency_format.description: The aggregate controlling the appearance of the currency with regard to comma and decimal.

decimal_places.description: This enumerated value controls the display of the decimal value, for example, 1.00. The default is 2 which means 2 decimals are displayed to the right of the decimal point, but you can specify 0 (zero) if you don’t want’ decimals to be displayed.

decimal_separator.description: This enumerated value controls the display of the decimal point, for example, 1.00 or 1,00. The default is Period but you could alternatively specify a value of Comma.

thousand_separator.description: This enumerated value controls how the thousandth’s place is separated from the next thousand, for example, 1,000,000. The default is Comma, as shown, but you can replace this with one of these values: Period, Space, Apostrophe .

thousand_separator_grouping.description: This enumerated value controls how the display of the currency value is grouped, for example, 10,000,000. The default is XX_XXX_XXX but you could replace this with X_XX_XX_XXX

QuickBooks doesn't page this query: at most this many records come back, in one answer, with no sign of whether more matched. class_ref.description:

A `class_ref` points to one class; if both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level `class_ref` is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`override_check_number`, `override_class_ref`, `override_memo`, `payment_txn_id`, `payment_txn_line_id`), or the set (`account_ref`, `amount`, `check_number`, `class_ref`, `entity_ref`, `memo`, `payment_method_ref`). full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

def_macro.description: `def_macro` lets you assign a reusable name to a returned `txn_id` or `txn_line_id` so later requests can reference it with `useMacro`. This feature requires SDK 2.0+.

include_line_items.description: This filter allows you to omit line items from a query response to get a smaller result. The default value is false, so line items are omitted by default. Set `include_line_items` to true to include line items in the response if you don’t mind getting a larger result.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. On by default, with pages of 100 records (25 with `include_line_items`); send `iterator=true` with `max_returned` for another size. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

max_returned.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.) If you include a `max_returned` value, it must be at least 1.

The page size, with `iterator=true`. Sent without `iterator`, or with `iterator=false`, it's a cap instead: at most this many records come back, in one answer, and QuickBooks doesn't say whether more matched.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

meta_data.description: Use the `meta_data` attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). Counts are approximate and may vary slightly if records are created or deleted during processing.

modified_date_range_filter.description:
Filters according to the dates when transactions were last modified. The `modified_date_range_filter` aggregate isn’t required to contain any elements, but if it is empty, we recommend that you leave it out altogether. Note that the time portion of the `from_modified_date` and `to_modified_date` fields wasn’t supported in qbXML version 1.0 or 1.1.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

from_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00.

to_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or before this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to end-of-day (23:59:59).

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

from_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or after this date. Both `from_txn_date` and `to_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999.If you omit `from_txn_date`, it will be set to 1970-01-01 (1969-12-31 PST).

to_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or before this date. Both `to_txn_date` and `from_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999. If you omit `to_txn_date`, it will be set to 2038-01-19 (2038-01-18 PST).

date_macro.description: `date_macro` filters by transaction date (not last-modified date). Do not combine `date_macro` with `from_modified_date`/`to_modified_date` in the same query filter set.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `full_name` or `list_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `entity_filter`, `item_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

account_ref.description: `account_ref` points to an account in the company file. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. Meaning depends on context: for checks it is the funding account; for ExpenseLineAdd it may be required by accounting preferences; for credit-card transactions it identifies the bank or card account involved.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A `class_ref` points to one class; if both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level `class_ref` is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

Filters by `ref_number` range. Numeric-only bounds are compared numerically; otherwise comparison is lexicographic.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `paid_status`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

from_ref_number.description: The first `ref_number` in the search range. If `from_ref_number` is omitted, the range will begin with first number on the list.

to_ref_number.description: The final `ref_number` in the search range. If `to_ref_number` is omitted, the range will end with last number on the list.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

txn_date_range_filter.description:
Filters according to the original transaction dates.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `paid_status`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

from_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or after this date. Both `from_txn_date` and `to_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999.If you omit `from_txn_date`, it will be set to 1970-01-01 (1969-12-31 PST).

to_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or before this date. Both `to_txn_date` and `from_txn_date` must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999. If you omit `to_txn_date`, it will be set to 2038-01-19 (2038-01-18 PST).

date_macro.description: `date_macro` filters by transaction date (not last-modified date). Do not combine `date_macro` with `from_modified_date`/`to_modified_date` in the same query filter set.

txn_id.description:
`txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `paid_status`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). ar_account_ref.description: `ar_account_ref` points to an Accounts Receivable account. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

bill_address.description: This aggregate supports at most five address lines. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in `ship_address_block` or `bill_address_block`.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided in `sales_tax_code_ref`, `full_name` is ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

serial_number.description:
The serial number of the asset.

Choose at most one of: `serial_number`, or `lot_number`.

service_date.description: Indicates the date on which the QuickBooks user performs the service for the customer.

txn_line_id.description: Identification number of the transaction line. (`txn_line_id` is supported as of v2.0 of the SDK. With qbXML v1.0 and v1.1, `txn_line_id` is always returned as zero.) If you need to add a new transaction line in a transaction Mod request, you can do so by setting the `txn_line_id` to -1.

unit_of_measure.description: In a transaction line item, the name of the unit of measure selected from within the item’s available units. If the company file is enabled only for single unit of measure per item, this must be the base unit!

is_pending.description: If `is_pending` is set to true, the invoice hasn’t been completed. Pending sales might include unpaid orders, estimates, tracked hours that haven’t yet been billed, or sales of back-ordered items.

is_tax_included.description: For future use with international versions of QuickBooks.

is_to_be_emailed.description: When enabled, QuickBooks validates the customer email at runtime before sending. If no valid email is available, the request fails.

is_to_be_printed.description: If `is_to_be_printed` is true, QuickBooks queues the form for later printing. It does not print immediately; printing is still a user action in QuickBooks.

item_sales_tax_ref.description: An ItemSalesTax entry represents one tax rate paid to one tax agency. Use it when a transaction needs a single tax calculation. For multi-rate scenarios, use a sales-tax group instead. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided for `item_sales_tax_ref`, `list_id` is used.

memo.description: Message that appears in reports, but not on the invoice.

other.description: Other, Other1, and Other2 are built-in transaction custom fields. Other is transaction-level; Other1 and Other2 are line-level. ref_number.description: `ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

ship_date.description: The date when the product was, or will be, shipped.

ship_method_ref.description: A shipping method, for example, standard mail or overnight delivery. A `ship_method_ref` aggregate refers to an item on the ShipMethod list. In a request, if a `ship_method_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

When you create a price level, you must specify whether it is a fixed percentage or a per item price level. Once you create the price level, you can’t change this. QuickBooks Pro and greater versions support fixed percentages, but only QuickBooks Premier and Enterprise support the per item price level. Where is this discount applied if Price Levels are enabled in QuickBooks preferences?

Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

price_level_per_item.description: Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

adjust_percentage.description:
If you don’t want to apply a custom price (for price levels) or custom rate (for billing rates), you can apply an adjusted price discount using the pair of fields `adjust_percentage` and `adjust_relative_to` (AdjustBillingRateRelativeTo for billing rates).

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

adjust_relative_to.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a flat custom price (flat amount or percentage) or you could use PriceLevelAdjustment to apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (`custom_price`) or a fixed discount percentage (`custom_price_percent`). Alternatively, instead of a flat custom price or discount, you could apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price_percent.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (`custom_price`) or a fixed discount percentage (`custom_price_percent`).

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

item_ref.description: `item_ref` may accept all item types or a restricted subset, depending on the request. Examples: PurchaseOrder and Bill do not allow discount or sales-tax items; VehicleMileageAdd requires a service or other-charge item; BillingRateAdd requires a service item. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level `class_ref` is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

expected_date.description: The date on which shipment is expected.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

fob.description: QuickBooks uses the term FOB, “freight on board,” to indicate the place from which the product is shipped. The FOB has no accounting implications.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

An entity refers to a person on the QuickBooks Customer list, Vendor list, Employee list, or Other Names list. You can use an EntityQuery request to get information about all the entities that are set up in the QuickBooks file. In an ARRefundCreditCard query, this must be a customer/customer job.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. list_id_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants.

full_name_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants. For names that don’t have children, `full_name_with_children` is exactly the same as `full_name`.

include_line_items.description: This filter allows you to omit line items from a query response to get a smaller result. The default value is false, so line items are omitted by default. Set `include_line_items` to true to include line items in the response if you don’t mind getting a larger result.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. On by default, with pages of 100 records (25 with `include_line_items`); send `iterator=true` with `max_returned` for another size. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

max_returned.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.) If you include a `max_returned` value, it must be at least 1.

The page size, with `iterator=true`. Sent without `iterator`, or with `iterator=false`, it's a cap instead: at most this many records come back, in one answer, and QuickBooks doesn't say whether more matched.

Note that the time portion of the `from_modified_date` and `to_modified_date` fields wasn’t supported in qbXML version 1.0 or 1.1.

from_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. credit_card_txn_input_info_mod.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info_mod.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

iterator.description: Page through every match: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. On by default, with pages of 100 records (25 with `include_line_items` or `include_linked_txns`); send `iterator=true` with `max_returned` for another size. Off when you send `iterator=false` (every match in one answer) or `max_returned` alone (at most that many, in one answer). It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.

max_returned.description:

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

ship_date.description: The date when the product was, or will be, shipped.

ship_method_ref.description: A shipping method, for example, standard mail or overnight delivery. A `ship_method_ref` aggregate refers to an item on the ShipMethod list. In a request, if a `ship_method_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list family, not across the company file: customers, vendors, employees and other names share one sequence, every item type shares another, and each other list has its own.

template_ref.description: QuickBooks templates specify how to print certain transactions. A template query returns the names of all templates that have been defined in QuickBooks. A `template_ref` element refers to one of these templates.

txn_date.description: The date of the transaction. In some cases, if you leave `txn_date` out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill `txn_date` with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

bill_address.description: This aggregate supports at most five address lines. You can provide a structured address (Addr1-Addr3 plus City/State/`postal_code`/etc.) or use block mode (Addr1-Addr5 only). Do not mix block mode with other address fields. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in `ship_address_block` or `bill_address_block`.
